items.title: Dollar weaker as Fed-fueled rally stalls; lower US yields help yen
points: NEW YORK, - The US dollar eased across the board on Friday as a weeks-long rally fueled by bets on a hawkish Federal Reserve lost momentum, but waning appetite for riskier currencies kept the dollar's losses in check.
The dollar index fell 0.1% to 103.86, just short of the 103.9 level it touched in the previous session, its highest since April 2025.
The index was on track to snap an eight-session winning streak and is up 1.9% so far this month.

The dollar's rally accelerated on November 10, when hotter-than-expected US inflation data reinforced bets that the Fed would tighten policy and Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a 50-basis-point hike in December should be considered.
The dollar slipped 0.5% against the franc.

Japan's annual core inflation accelerated to 2.2% in October, staying above the central bank's 2% target for a second straight month and pointing to broadening price pressures that strengthen the case for a near-term rate hike by the Bank of Japan.

“Yesterday’s AI IPO is a valuation test, and with the 10-year around 5% and the Fed still hiking, investors are asking how much of the AI story is already priced in,” said Gene Goldman, chief investment officer at Cetera, El Segundo, California.
Friday’s action highlights the shift in fortunes on Wall Street since the Nasdaq hit its last high on October 6.

IVF specialist Dr Krishnaveni said that they opted ovulation induction as a first line of treatment, which is not a In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) method.
Currently, over 500 couples have rolled for treatments at the government hospitals IVF centre.

items.title: Following Cyclone Akvan, monsoon rain to resume over T.N. from tomorrow
points: Heavy rainfall is set to persist in interior districts till November 26, say RMC officials. | Photo Credit: R.
RAGU Following Cyclone Akvan’s passage on Friday morning, most parts of Tamil Nadu are likely to experience a brief break in monsoon activity, accompanied by a dip in night-time temperatures.
The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) has also forecast ground frost at isolated places in the Nilgiris and Kodaikanal till Sunday.
The State has so far received nearly 26 cm of monsoon rainfall, which is 14% lower than its seasonal share since October 1.

Durai, Head, Regional Weather Forecasting Centre, RMC, said dry and cold northwesterly winds and the absence of cloud cover and rainfall led to a rise in day temperatures and drop in minimum temperatures over most parts of the State.
While coastal districts are expected to benefit more, interior Tamil Nadu is also likely to receive moderate rainfall till November 26.
On Monday, rainfall is expected to intensify over 10 coastal districts, including Cuddalore, Thoothukudi, and Kanniyakumari.

items.title: KRRS demands action against sugar factory
points: Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha leaders have alleged that the Malaprabha Cooperative Sugar Factory, headed by Channaraj Hattiholi, an MLC and Congress leader, had betrayed farmers by deliberately delaying crushing operations.

points: The Madras High Court has questioned the Tamil Nadu government over its decision to abandon the proposed greenfield airport at Parandur, asking why the project was scrapped midway after receiving approvals following detailed studies and after substantial…

items.title: Stubble Smoke Causes Fatal Crash In Punjab's Doraha, Woman Dies, 3 Injured
points: A woman was killed, and her husband and two other men were injured after thick smoke from a paddy stubble fire allegedly caused a car to collide with two motorcycles on a village link road near Jaipura village in Doraha on Friday, police said.
The woman who died has been identified as Manjit Kaur, 55, a resident of Shahpur.
Her husband was seriously injured and was referred to Dayanand Medical College and Hospital (DMCH) in Ludhiana.
The two other injured, Jaspal Singh and Surinder Singh, both residents of Payal, were being treated at a private hospital in Doraha.
According to preliminary information, a farmer, identified as Gurdeep Singh, had allegedly set fire to paddy stubble in his field along the link road.

items.title: UP's Jobless Growth Paradox: Why Workers Still Migrate Despite Economic Boom
points: Yet a paradox remains: why are workers still leaving the state in large numbers, particularly from a concentrated cluster of districts in eastern Uttar Pradesh?
According to a study published in the International Journal of Novel Research and Development (IJNRD), the state's growth has not translated into proportionate employment gains.
More than 48 per cent of Uttar Pradesh's workforce remains dependent on agriculture, even though the sector contributed only 27 per cent to the state's Gross State Value Added (GSVA) in 2024-25.
Employment elasticity has remained near zero or negative across most sectors between 2010 and 2025, reinforcing concerns about jobless growth.
During FY21-25, a 10 per cent increase in Uttar Pradesh's economic output generated only 1.8 per cent additional employment.
Manufacturing, despite attracting substantial investment, generated just 2.2 per cent more jobs for every 10 per cent increase in output.

items.title: SEBI plans further easing of FPI rules, targets five-day onboarding
points: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) plans to further ease compliance requirements for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), including removing certain conditions that are not prevalent in other major markets, Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on…

items.title: Delhi Police bans laser lights at weddings, parties near IGI Airport for 60 days over pilot safety concerns
points: Delhi Police has prohibited the use of laser beams during weddings, parties and other celebrations in areas falling under the Palam subdivision of the Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport, citing the risk of pilots getting distracted while landing…

The order, issued by Assistant Commissioner of Police Pradeep Kumar Meena under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, came into effect on November 18 and will remain in force till January 16, 2027.
According to the order, the Air Traffic Control (ATC) at IGI Airport had reported several incidents of pilots experiencing visual distraction due to laser beams, particularly while landing aircrafts.
Such incidents not only cause nuisance but can also pose a serious threat to the safety of passengers, crew members and aircraft, it read.

The police said several farmhouses, banquet halls, hotels and restaurants had come up in and around the airport area, where bright lights, including laser beams, were frequently used during marriage functions, parties and other events.
